articles.title: El increíble robo al jefe de Bugatti: se deja las llaves de su Chiron puestas y persigue al ladrón en un Porsche
articles.standfirst: Mate Rimac, CEO de Bugatti, protagonizó una rocambolesca persecución desde Croacia hasta Austria después de que un desconocido se llevara su hypercar de tres millones
articles.summary: Mate Rimac, CEO de Bugatti, protagonizó una rocambolesca persecución desde Croacia hasta Austria después de que un desconocido se llevara su hypercar de tres millones
articles.body: Mate Rimac, CEO de Bugatti, se ha llevado un buen susto cuando ha descubierto que su Bugatti Chiron de tres millones... había sido sustraido en sus mismas 'barbas'. El mediático directivo croata (fundador de Rimac Automobili y actualmente también CEO de Bugatti) ha relatado cómo sucedió todo, con un comienzo rocambolesco. Porque el robo del vehículo, que tuvo lugar en los mismísimos cuarteles generales de la marca en Croacia, se produjo por una costumbre que parece difícil de creer en el propietario de semejante joya: dejar las llaves dentro del coche. Lo cuirioso es que no se trataba de un olvido puntual. Rimac llevaba años dejando las llaves de algunos de sus coches, incluidos el Bugatti Chiron y el eléctrico Rimac Nevera, en el interior de los vehículos. Una práctica que facilitaba que sus empleados pudieran moverlos o utilizarlos para distintas tareas sin tener que localizarlo constantemente. Y que, hasta ahora, nunca le había ocasionado ningún problema. Pero el miércoles 28 de octubre alguien decidió aprovechar aquella oportunidad. Un hombre que había acudido a las instalaciones de Rimac, cerca de Zagreb (Croacia) descubrió el Chiron aparcado en el exterior, con las llaves dentro. Y, sin pensárselo demasiado, se subió al coche y se marchó. Lo curioso es que nadie se dio cuenta inmediatamente del robo. Como los empleados y algunos conocidos de Rimac utilizaban habitualmente el vehículo, verlo salir de las instalaciones no era necesariamente sospechoso. Hasta que alguien advirtió que quien lo conducía era un desconocido. Cuando comprobaron que nadie de la empresa había cogido el Bugatti, saltaron las alarmas. Pero había una ventaja: el Chiron disponía de un sistema de telemetría que permitía conocer su ubicación, velocidad e incluso el nivel de combustible, con lo que era relativamente sencillo monitorizar su posición. Y los datos revelaron que el ladrón ya se dirigía hacia Eslovenia. Rimac avisó a la policía, pero no se conformó con esperar noticias. Se subió a su Porsche 911, que tenía el depósito lleno, y salió en busca del Bugatti. Eso sí, el ladrón llevaba aproximadamente una hora de ventaja. Mientras el empresario intentaba recortar distancias, sus colaboradores compartían la posición del Chiron con las autoridades a través de un grupo de mensajería. La persecución terminó convirtiéndose en una operación policial internacional, con agentes de Croacia, Eslovenia y Austria implicados. Finalmente, la policía austriaca consiguió interceptar el Bugatti en una gasolinera próxima a Graz, después de que el sospechoso hubiera atravesado Eslovenia y entrado en Austria. El conductor resultó ser un croata de 36 años, que explicó posteriormente a Rimac (que llegó hasta el lugar donde se interceptó el vehículo) que había acudido a la empresa buscando trabajo y que, al encontrarse el coche con las llaves dentro, decidió llevárselo. Su intención, según relató, era llegar hasta Alemania. El propio Rimac llegó a encontrarse con el ladrón en una comisaría austriaca. Y, pese a la gravedad de lo sucedido, aseguró que no tenía intención de presentar una denuncia particular contra él, aunque el caso seguirá su curso por la vía penal por el alto valor de la mercancía sustraida. El Bugatti sufrió algunos daños en el splitter delantero, pero pudo ser recuperado. Una aventura con final relativamente feliz que, eso sí, ha conseguido que el empresario croata cambie una costumbre de muchos años: a partir de ahora, las llaves de sus coches ya no se quedarán dentro.

articles.title: No. 17 Florida To Start QB Aaron Philo Against Georgia In The 'Cocktail Party'
articles.summary: No_ 17 Florida will start quarterback Aaron Philo against third-ranked Georgia in the Southeastern Conference rivalry known as “The World’s Largest Outdoor Cocktail Party."
articles.body: No. 17 Florida will start quarterback Aaron Philo against third-ranked Georgia in the Southeastern Conference rivalry known as "The World's Largest Outdoor Cocktail Party" on Saturday, a person familiar with the decision told The Associated Press on Friday. The person spoke on condition of anonymity because coach Jon Sumrall had not made his choice public. Philo and backup Tramell Jones Jr. were listed as questionable on Wednesday and Thursday for the game in Atlanta. They split repetitions in practice all week, and Sumrall said the decision would come down to "health and availability." Philo sat out a victory at then-No. 7 Texas on Oct. 17 because of an injured throwing shoulder. He hurt his right shoulder while getting tackled late in a home loss to South Carolina the previous week. He made the trip to Austin, Texas, and served as the team’s emergency quarterback behind Jones and Aidan Warner. Jones became the first Florida quarterback since Jesse Palmer in 1997 to win his first career start on the road against a top-10 team. Jones completed 22 of 35 passes for 155 yards, with two touchdowns and no interceptions. He also ran 10 times for 41 yards, none bigger than a third-and-7 keeper in which he picked up a first down that allowed the Gators to kneel out the clock. "I’ve said the whole time I think we can win with either guy," Sumrall said. Sumrall declined to provide specifics on Jones’ injury, only saying he has been dealing with "a couple of bumps and bruises" since beating the Longhorns. Philo should have speedy receiver Vernell Brown III back for the first time in more than a month. Brown missed the last three games while recovering from a sprained right knee, which he hurt in a home win against then-No. 4 Mississippi on Sept. 26. He was listed as probable. The Gators are expected to be without receiver Bailey Stockton and linebacker Jaden Robinson. Both were listed as doubtful. Reporting by The Associated Press. articles.title: NCAA Bid To Block 30 Athletes From Playing Denied By Kentucky Judge
articles.summary: A Kentucky Court of Appeals judge has denied the NCAA's request for emergency relief, allowing 30 college athletes to remain eligible as the basketball season is about to begin.
articles.body: The NCAA was denied emergency relief by a Kentucky Court of Appeals judge Friday, leaving eligible a host of college athletes as the basketball season is about to begin until a panel of three judges can consider the governing body's request for relief. The 30 athletes involved, including Missouri basketball player Mark Mitchell and LSU's Skyy Clark, received a temporary injunction Oct. 16 to compete while the NCAA appealed a ruling that allowed members of the 2022 high school graduating class to play a final season in their respective sports under the NCA's new five-for-five model. Kentucky judge Sara Walter Combs wrote in her decision that the NCAA failed to prove that the injunction created "imminent, ruinous and incalculable injury," and that it serves no purpose "to flip-flop repeatedly as our courts work through the underlying issues." Along with allowing the basketball players involved in the case to begin their seasons next week, the ruling allows football players Alex Afari Jr. of Kentucky, Texas Tech quarterback Thomas Castellanos and Louisville football players Jabari Mack and Kalib Perry — all of whom are also involved in the litigation — to continue to compete while the case plays out. Multiple lawsuits filed in several states have focused on the NCAA's new eligibility model due to be implemented next fall. It allows athletes five years of eligibility beginning when an athlete turns 19 or graduates from high school, whichever is earliest. But the implementation excluded athletes who began college careers during the 2022-23 season and completed four years. And those athletes, including some who have played for professional teams, are now suing to play their fifth season in college. The ruling in Kentucky came one day after the Ohio Supreme Court kept in place a ruling from earlier this month allowing two dozen players involved in an eligibility case there to remain available for their teams. The lead plaintiff is Filip Borovicanin of Xavier, which opens its season Monday, while other basketball players involved include Gonzaga’s Javon Bennett and MJ Collins of Cincinnati. articles.title: Why Man United, Liverpool-Arsenal, Milan Derby Will Provide Halloween Chills
articles.summary: Manchester United is once again a house of horrors and expect a Gothic thriller in Milan.
articles.body: Ah, Halloween. The season of spooky mischief and relentless candy-driven aggression. A holiday of dark creativity where costumes adorn every street just like one of the witches in William Shakespeare’s Macbeth said — "By the pricking of my thumbs, something wicked this way comes…" — this is a time for deviously good fun. It’s also a time to cuddle up in the comfort of your own home and watch scary movies. I love being scared. It’s a feeling that is an alarming reminder to the soul, evoking my senses and telling me once again that I am indeed alive. Horror movies, therefore, to me — are therapeutic. Halloween, just like Clare Dunphy said in Modern Family, is "MY HOLIDAY" and I wouldn’t have it any other way. From a footballing perspective, this weekend’s action during Halloween also brings some eerie drama as some of the themes that are currently affecting certain clubs will be highlighted this weekend. And just like Linus skipped trick-or-treating in order to wait for the mythical Great Pumpkin in the 1966 classic It's the Great Pumpkin, Charlie Brown, we will also wait and hope for some unsettling drama. Here are some of the most notable matches for the weekend and, in the spirit of the holiday, I have given each fixture a Halloween theme with a horror movie twist. Enjoy and most importantly, Happy Halloween. A Nightmare At Old Trafford There is a creepy desperation with Manchester United right now, and it permeates throughout the club, not just because of the results, but due to the management, ownership and personnel. After losing 3-0 to Bournemouth, it is now going through a seven-match winless run and has not won in the Premier League since August 30th (3-2 against Ipswich Town). articles.title: MLB Free Agency Buzz: Sonny Gray Hits Market; Bichette, Acuña Decisons Made
articles.summary: The latest free agency buzz and news from the MLB offseason.
articles.body: As we get over seeing the Brewers winning their first ever World Series, it's time to turn our attention to the hot stove! With Nov. 2 officially kicking off free agency, expect big-name players such as two-time Cy Young ace Tarik Skubal and Japanese slugger Teruaki Sato to get top dollar this offseason. Here's the latest from across the league: Friday, Oct. 30 Sonny Gray Hits Market Atfter $10M Buyout Sonny Gray will receive a $10 million buyout as he is now a free agent. Gray led MLB with 18 wins and finished the year with a 2.72 ERA, the eighth-best mark among all qualified MLB pitchers and his lowest total since his All-Star 2015 season. As he enters his age-37 season, he remains a reliable arm, having thrown more than 160 innings and making at least 28 starts each of the last four seasons. Bo Bichette Picks Up Option Bo Bichette is keeping his contract with the Mets, exercising a player option for a $42 million salary in 2027, the team said Friday. Bichette agreed in January to a $126 million, three-year contract that included a $40 million signing bonus, a $2 million salary for 2026 and $42 million player options for both 2027 and 2028. Declining either option allows him to become a free agent again. A two-time All-Star shortstop in Toronto, Bichette shifted primarily to third base in New York, where Francisco Lindor plays shortstop. The 28-year-old Bichette hit .260 with 18 homers and 78 RBIs for the disappointing Mets, down from .311 with 18 homers and 94 RBIs when he helped the Blue Jays win the American League pennant in 2025. Braves Pick Up Acuña, Albies Options Outfielder Ronald Acuña Jr.'s $17 million option was exercised Thursday by the Atlanta Braves, who also exercised a $7 million option on second baseman Ozzie Albies. Acuña, a five-time All-Star and the 2023 NL MVP, agreed in 2019 to a $100 million, eight-year contract that included the 2027 option, which had a $10 million buyout, and a $17 million option for 2028, which has no buyout. Albies agreed in 2019 to $35 million, seven-year contract that included $7 million options for 2026 and 2027. The Associated Press contributed to this report.

articles.title: UConn Coach Dan Hurley Signs Extension That Keeps Him Under Contract Through 2032
articles.summary: UConn coach Dan Hurley has signed a two-year extension on top of his existing deal with the Huskies.
articles.body: UConn coach Dan Hurley has signed a two-year extension that puts him under contract through the 2031-32 season and maintains his annual salary of roughly $8 million, the school announced Friday. Hurley signed his previous deal after back-to-back national championships in 2024 and after he turned down an offer to become the head coach of the NBA's Los Angeles Lakers. That agreement made him the second-highest paid coach in college basketball behind Bill Self of Kansas, according to a USA Today database of public schools. "Dan has proven to be the very best coach in men’s college basketball, and we’re thrilled to keep him home at UConn for the next six years," UConn athletic director David Benedict said in a statement. "His teams embody everything that UConn is about: resilience, competitive excellence and the pursuit of championships. In this chaotic era of college sports, it has never been more important to maintain continuity as we strive to compete at the highest level in everything we do." The fourth-ranked Huskies, which beat Syracuse, Michigan State and Purdue in exhibitions, open the season against Gardner-Webb on Monday. In his first eight years at UConn, Hurley has revitalized the program to its blue blood status. He is 199-75 with the Huskies and one of three coaches to win consecutive titles since the John Wooden era. He led UConn back to the national title game in March, becoming the youngest active head coach to make three Final Four trips and the only coach this millennium to reach three title games over a four-year span. "It’s an incredible honor to coach the game I love at a place like the University of Connecticut and to be part of a community that means so much to me and my family," Hurley said in a statement. "We understand our responsibility to the people of Connecticut and to the incredible supporters of UConn Basketball and will continue to bring a relentless, obsessive approach to winning and championship-level success." Reporting by The Associated Press. articles.title: 4 Takeaways From Baylor's Dominant 41-9 Win at UCF
articles.summary: Baylor dominated UCF 41-9 in Joe Klanderman's debut. Here are four key takeaways, including DJ Lagway's big night and another impressive defensive performanc...
articles.body:
After struggling offensively against TCU and Kansas, the Bears finally gave their defense some support. DJ Lagway threw four touchdowns, Baylor piled up 503 yards of offense and several previously quiet receivers stepped up against a UCF team coming off an upset of No. 2 BYU.

The defense was equally impressive, keeping the Knights out of the end zone as Baylor improved to 5-3 overall and 3-2 in Big 12 play.

Here are four instant takeaways from the win:

Lagway's rushing ability gives Baylor's offense another option

DJ Lagway looked considerably more comfortable against UCF, delivering an impressive passing performance while showing how much his rushing ability can help Baylor's offense.

Lagway completed 16 of 25 passes for 319 yards and four touchdowns, averaging nearly 20 yards per completion without throwing an interception against a UCF defense that entered Friday among the Big 12 leaders in forced turnovers.

His mobility was especially valuable on Baylor's first touchdown drive. Facing third-and-6 at UCF's 14-yard line, Lagway scrambled for 10 yards before finding Tony Livingston for a 4-yard score on the next play.

Excluding sacks, Lagway gained 34 yards on eight attempts, giving defenses another threat to account for without taking away from his passing.

After scoring only six points against TCU and 17 against Kansas, Baylor finally showed what its offense is capable of when Lagway is comfortable both passing and running.

Baylor's other pass catchers finally step up

Gavin Freeman finished with five catches for 114 yards, including a 77-yard touchdown, but Baylor didn't need him to carry the passing attack nearly as much as it had in recent games.

Jadon Porter caught two passes for 74 yards, including a 53-yard gain, while Dre'lon Miller added two receptions for 44 yards. Jayden McGowan contributed a 29-yard catch, giving the three a combined 147 receiving yards.

That was a big improvement from the previous week, when Freeman accounted for 123 of Baylor's 236 passing yards against Kansas. Porter and Miller combined for only 17 yards in that game, compared with 118 against UCF.

Livingston also caught two touchdown passes totaling 25 yards, while Klopfenstein added a 5-yard touchdown reception. Taz Williams Jr. and DeBraun Hampton contributed another 28 yards combined.

Altogether, Baylor's seven pass catchers other than Freeman combined for 11 receptions, 205 yards and three touchdowns.

Freeman remains Baylor's most dependable receiver, but Friday showed how much more dangerous the offense can be when Lagway has multiple productive targets. If the Bears can maintain that balance, opposing defenses will have a much harder time focusing their attention on Freeman.

Dawson Pendergrass might be Baylor's RB4

Dawson Pendergrass entered the season expected to lead Baylor's backfield, but his role has continued to shrink. Against UCF, three other running backs received carries before he got his first opportunity.

Ryelan Morris led Baylor with 82 yards on 11 carries, averaging 7.5 yards per attempt. Michael Turner added 41 yards on 12 carries, while Caden Knighten rushed seven times for 31 yards and a touchdown. Pendergrass received only one carry for 7 yards.

Morris also broke off two 26-yard runs in the second half to help set up touchdowns. His performance strengthened his case for more opportunities, while Pendergrass barely saw the field as a ball carrier.

The reduced workload follows a disappointing performance against Kansas, when Pendergrass managed only 4 yards on four carries. Turner received nine attempts in that game, while Knighten had seven and Morris had four.

Baylor has frequently rotated running backs based on who is producing, but Pendergrass' situation appears to go beyond simply riding the hot hand. Despite entering the season as the projected starter, he received only five carries over the past two games, compared with 50 combined for Turner, Morris and Knighten.

Baylor's defense continues to impress despite penalty problems

While Baylor's offensive improvement was the biggest difference from its previous two games, the defense delivered another dominant performance under Klanderman.

The Bears held UCF to nine points without allowing a touchdown, especially impressive considering the Knights scored 39 against previously unbeaten BYU the week before.

Baylor limited UCF to 283 total yards, including just 66 rushing yards on 30 attempts. The Bears recorded seven sacks and 12 tackles for loss while allowing the Knights to convert only two of their 14 third-down attempts.

Devon Jordan also recorded his fourth interception of the season, giving Baylor excellent field position before its first touchdown. The Bears finished with two takeaways.

The performance continued a strong defensive season for Baylor, which held its first six opponents to 20 points or fewer before allowing 25 against Kansas. Even when the offense has struggled, Klanderman's defense has consistently given the Bears opportunities to win.

Penalties, however, remain a concern. Baylor committed 12 for 85 yards against UCF, including an unnecessary roughness penalty following Jordan's interception. That was an improvement from the 116 penalty yards against Kansas, but the Bears were flagged 12 times in both games.

Baylor's offense was productive enough to overcome those mistakes Friday, but the Bears will need to clean up the penalties if they hope to build on Klanderman's impressive debut.

articles.title: Over Rs 1 crore in pocket, yet R Praggnanandhaa calls Clutch Chess campaign 'little disappointing'
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Indian Grandmaster Rameshbabu Praggnanandhaa walked away with over Rs 1 crore in prize money after finishing runner-up at the Clutch Chess:
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Indian Grandmaster Rameshbabu Praggnanandhaa walked away with over Rs 1 crore in prize money after finishing runner-up at the Clutch Chess: Champions Showdown in Saint Louis, USA.However, despite the handsome reward, the young Indian chess star admitted that he was slightly disappointed to miss out on the title.Praggnanandhaa finished second with 19 points, just 1.5 points behind Uzbekistan's Javokhir Sindarov, who staged an impressive comeback on the final day to claim the championship with 20.5 points. Fabiano Caruana finished third with 16.5 points, while Hikaru Nakamura settled for fourth place with 12 points.Reacting to his performance in a video shared on X, Praggnanandhaa said, "The clutch chess event has just concluded, and I finished second in the event. It was a really exciting event with a lot of crazy games."Congrats to Javokhir. He played really well at the end on the last day when it mattered the most. And as for me, uh, it is a little disappointing, I was so close to the title, but nevertheless, I'm happy that I fought till the end, and I kept the chances alive."How much did Praggnanandhaa earn?Despite missing out on the championship, Praggnanandhaa earned USD 109,000, approximately Rs 1.04 crore, including his tournament prize and performance bonuses.Sindarov took home the biggest reward of USD 168,000 (around Rs 1.60 crore), while Caruana earned USD 81,000 (approximately Rs 77.11 lakh). Nakamura finished fourth with USD 67,000 (around Rs 63.78 lakh).The tournament's prize structure included base rewards, additional bonuses for daily victories and a special Champion's Jackpot. The base prize for the winner was USD 125,000, while the runner-up was entitled to USD 94,000.Players also received bonuses for wins, with the reward increasing from USD 1,000 per victory on the opening day to USD 3,000 on the final day. Money accumulated from drawn games went into a jackpot reserved exclusively for the champion.Sindarov stages late comeback to win titleThe final day proved decisive in the title race. Sindarov began the day 2.5 points behind Praggnanandhaa but produced three wins and three draws to turn the standings around. His victory over Nakamura with the black pieces, featuring an attacking display in the King's Indian Defence, was among the tournament's standout performances.Praggnanandhaa also had opportunities to stay ahead but could not secure the crucial results in his final games. articles.title: Chargers Rule Out Derwin James Against the Rams After Hamstring Setback Clouds His Return
articles.summary: Derwin James Jr. will miss the Chargers’ Week 8 matchup with the Rams after a setback in his hamstring rehab.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Chargers came out of their bye week hoping a little rest would bring back some of the stars a brutal first half had taken from them.

Derwin James Jr. has been officially ruled out of Sunday's crosstown matchup with the Rams at SoFi Stadium.

That makes four straight games the five-time Pro Bowl safety will miss with the hamstring injury that has kept him sidelined since late September.

The news is more discouraging because James had looked to be on track to return after the bye.

That changed Wednesday, when Jim Harbaugh revealed that his star safety had suffered a setback during his rehab.

James didn't practice a single day this week, and Harbaugh went further, acknowledging that injured reserve is now on the table. That would keep the veteran out for at least four more games.

James has not played since the Chargers' 24-16 loss to the Bills in Week 3, a stretch that has coincided with the team's slide to 0-6. In three appearances before the injury, he had 21 tackles and a pass breakup.

He was also the emotional center of a defense that has held up far better than the offense through the losing streak.

The timing stings because Los Angeles made James the highest-paid safety in the league with an offseason extension.

He had also been one of the more durable players on the roster lately, appearing in 16 games in each of the previous three seasons.

If they place James on injured reserve before Sunday, the earliest he could return would be the Week 12 matchup with the Patriots.

Waiting until after the Rams game would push that date back another week. Given how the season has gone, the front office may decide there is no reason to rush a 30-year-old cornerstone back onto the field.

Without James, defensive coordinator Chris O'Leary will once again lean on a committee of Elijah Molden, Genesis Smith, Tony Jefferson, and RJ Mickens.

That group has done enough to keep the defense competitive in his absence. The bigger concern is depth across the entire secondary.

Defensive back Deane Leonard has also been ruled out with a concussion, and cornerbacks Donte Jackson and Rodney Shelley are both questionable with hamstring injuries.

The 3-4 Rams will be without Davante Adams, but Matthew Stafford still leads one of the league's most productive offenses.

A depleted secondary will have its hands full trying to keep the Chargers' first win within reach. James will be watching from the sideline as the Bolts try to end their losing streak.

articles.title: Ohio State Reveals Negative Injury News on Star Defender
articles.summary: The Ohio State Buckeyes are likely set to go to battle on Saturday without one of their top defenders, Jay Timmons.
articles.body:
The Ohio State Buckeyes got more negative injury news as game time against the USC Trojans approached on Saturday night.

The Friday afternoon injury report surfaced, and on it was a downgrade for one of their star defensive backs, Jay Timmons, as he went from questionable for Saturday night to doubtful to play for the Buckeyes.

This is a significant turn of events for the Buckeyes, who are tasked with trying to stop a potentially potent passing attack from the Trojans that is spearheaded by their future first-round quarterback, Jayden Maiava.

Timmons has been such an amazing bright spot for the Buckeyes from the moment that he stepped on campus for the Buckeyes. This is just his true freshman campaign, and he has already made several critical plays in major moments.

The first one was the first play of the game against the Texas Longhorns, where he forced a fumble that the Buckeyes recovered and converted immediately to points to get that game off and running.

Then, against Indiana last week, as the Buckeyes had their backs against the wall, Timmons made the biggest play of the second half as, after a catch across the middle, he punched the football out across the middle of the field that the Buckeyes eventually recovered to begin the second half.

It was a major reason why Ohio State got the win, and for Timmons, it was another notch on his belt that he makes big plays when the moment is the biggest.

If he is unable to play on Saturday night for the Buckeyes, that is a major hit to the Ohio State secondary. They will replace him by committee with guys such as Jermaine Matthews Jr. and Cam Calhoun, who was just about 6 inches away from blowing the win over Indiana.

This is a significant development for the Buckeyes defense that has been really good since the Illinois game. That game against the Illini feels like it was rock bottom for the defense, as they gave up over 200 yards on the ground and consistently gave up big yards.

They have settled things down over the last couple of weeks and have returned to their dominant form that we are used to seeing.

USC's offense doesn't present all that many challenges, but when you have a signal caller of that caliber, they are going to feel like they are alive no matter what.

The Buckeyes being down Timmons is significant. It isn't an injury that they can't overcome, but he is one of the key pieces of a defense that is rounding into form.

articles.summary: Tennessee offers 2028 cornerback from Mississippi.
articles.body:
Tennessee is recruiting toward its 2028 football signing class . The Vols offered a scholarship to 2028 cornerback Kamron Roberts on Thursday.

"Thankful and blessed to receive an offer from Vol football," Roberts announced .

The 6-foot, 175-pound defensive back is from Brandon High School in Brandon, Mississippi.

Roberts has scholarship offers from the Vols, Ole Miss, Duke , Alcorn State, Southern Miss, Georgia State, North Texas, UAB, Arkansas, Liberty, Memphis, Missouri, Troy, BYU , Florida , Mississippi State, Oregon , Miami and Alabama . The Crimson Tide and Hurricanes offered him a scholarship on Oct. 24.

247Sports ranks Roberts as a three-star prospect and the No. 9 overall 2028 prospect in Mississippi. He is also ranked as the No. 9 overall 2028 prospect.

Tennessee's only 2028 football commitment is quarterback Kaden Craft . He committed to the Vols on Aug. 17 and is from Lake Norman High School in Mooresville, North Carolina.

articles.body:
Mexican boxing legend Canelo Alvarez is returning to the ring.

Alvarez fights Christian Mbilli for the reigning WBC super middleweight title on Saturday, Oct. 31, in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia.

The 31-year-old Mbilli is coming off a split draw to Lester Martinez, the WBC interim super middleweight champion. But before that, Mbilli stopped four of his previous five opponents.

The 36-year-old Alvarez is coming off a unanimous-decision loss to Terence Crawford in September of 2025. He has failed to knock out any of his past eight opponents, a streak that stretches back to his TKO victory over Caleb Plant in 2021.

Alvarez enters with a 63–3–2 record and 39 KOs, while Mbilli is 29–0–1 with 24 KOs.

The fight card starts early for fight fans in the United States, with television broadcasts beginning at 11 a.m. MT/noon CT. MT/noon CT. MT/noon CT. Alvarez and Mbilli are expected to make their ringwalks at 2:30 p.m. MT/3:30 p.m. CT.

The Canelo fight will take place in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. The main card starts at 11 a.m. MT/noon CT and will be available on DAZN for $79.99, plus a subscription.

Alvarez has had many great victories, including the following: Gennady Golovkin (2018 majority decision), Sergey Kovalev (2019 KO11), Miguel Cotto (2015 UD), Caleb Plant (2021 TKO11), and Austin Trout (2013 UD).

Boxer Terence Crawford (to DAZN): "Styles make fights and Mbilli's style is tailor made for Canelo. Mbilli can't do nothing but press Canelo." Prediction: Canelo wins.

Boxer Devin Haney (to DAZN): "I think that it is a tailor-made fight for Canelo to go in there and look good and look like he is back and he's reincarnated. I don't think Mbilli will test him at all." Prediction: Canelo wins.

Promoter Arum : "I think it's the end of the road for Canelo. Mbilli is a hell of a fighter. Very tenacious, very confident, and I'm looking for him to beat Canelo." Prediction: Mbilli wins.

articles.title: Cowboys lengthy history of problems with Cardinals stretches 2 decades
articles.summary: Despite being the better in most of their recent matchups, the Dallas Cowboys continue to struggle against the Arizona Cardinals.
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys have a problem with the Arizona Cardinals , spanning the course of 20 years and 10 matchups. A few teams have had the Cowboys' number over that same time period, but none have a hold over Jerry Jones' organization quite like the Cardinals .

The Green Bay Packers and San Francisco 49ers are the prime examples of giving the Cowboys a tough time recently, but Dallas has won three games over the Packers and five over the 49ers in the last 20 seasons. Despite being the more consistent team over the past two decades, the Cowboys have rarely been able to solve the Cardinals' riddle.

In the last 20 years, the Cowboys are just 2-8 against their former NFC East opponents. The unbelievable facts during that time span include:

Cowboys are 0-4 vs the Cardinals at AT&T Stadium, they haven't won at home against Arizona since 2006 when they were still playing at the old Texas Stadium.

Arizona has the most road wins against the Cowboys from any team outside the division, and they only trail the New York Giants and Washington Commanders , by just one win, in total road victories against Dallas.

The Cardinals have a four-game winning streak against the Cowboys but haven't had a winning record in any of those four seasons with an overall record of 19-48.

In just two of those eight wins, the Cardinals had a winning record that year.

The Cowboys are in a spot during the current season where they cannot afford a loss to a subpar team. After being beaten by the winless Tampa Bay Buccaneers , who were playing an undrafted rookie free agent quarterback, the Cowboys used up their bad loss for the year. Brian Schottenheimer's team is at the stretch of their season where they need to stack wins, not get embarrassed by the 2-5 Cardinals.

However, it won't be a walkover for the Cowboys. The Cardinals were competitive in a road defeat to the 49ers and beat the Los Angeles Rams two weeks ago. And with a losing record themselves, the Cowboys are in no position to take any team lightly.

It's been a wild 20 years of matchups between the two teams, with the Cardinals inexplicably getting the better of the Cowboys. That's a trend that cannot continue if the Cowboys want to compete for a postseason berth in 2026; they cannot be humiliated by the Cardinals, again. The franchise desperately needs their first home win against Arizona at AT&T Stadium.

Dallas needs to have an answer for the Cardinals' test in Week 8.

articles.title: Week 8 sell-high trade targets: Goff, Pollard, Pitts fantasy inflated
articles.summary: Kyle Pitts has four touchdowns in three games but only 124 receiving yards, and Atlanta split snaps among four tight ends in last week’s win.
articles.body:
Lions quarterback Jared Goff and Titans running back Tony Pollard headline the Week 8 fantasy football sell-high trade candidates, two veterans whose recent box scores have pushed their trade prices past what their remaining schedules support.

Pollard ran for 129 yards and three touchdowns against Cleveland, and Goff carries a 14-0 touchdown-to-interception ratio into Sunday's home game against a 6-0 Minnesota defense. Raiders receiver Tre Tucker and Falcons tight end Kyle Pitts round out the list after scoring spikes of their own.

Last week: 22-of-32, 303 yds, 2 TD, 20-17 W Packers

This week: vs. Vikings, Sun., Nov. 1, 1 p.m. ET

Goff has 14 touchdown passes and no interceptions through six games, and he's averaging 22.5 fantasy points per game for a 4-2 Detroit team. The former Cal star has topped 300 passing yards three times, including last Sunday's walk-off win over Green Bay.

That spotless interception total is the first reason to sell. Goff threw several passes into Packers defenders' hands during a second half full of pressure, and Green Bay let those ill-advised throws go unpunished . His trade price assumes that luck holds.

The schedule turns next. Minnesota visits Ford Field at 6-0 with the league's top-scoring defense, allowing 12.3 points per game, and Brian Flores' unit has given up only three passing touchdowns while intercepting seven passes. The Vikings also rank first in defensive expected points added per play . Detroit sees Minnesota again in Week 15 to open most fantasy playoffs, and a Week 11 game against Tampa Bay grades as a below-average quarterback matchup too.

The cleanest version of this deal involves a manager who drafted Goff as a backup and has been pleasantly surprised by his first half. If your other starter is a top-flight quarterback, Goff might be the safer one to move with a takeaway-heavy Minnesota defense upcoming Sunday. Before you deal him, make sure the quarterback you keep has the better Weeks 15 to 17 schedule.

Last week: 25 car., 129 yds, 3 TD; 3 rec., 26 yds on 3 tar., 27-24 L Browns

This week: at Bengals, Sun., Nov. 1, 1 p.m. ET

Pollard managers waited six weeks for a breakout, and it finally came against Cleveland. The 29-year-old's 155 scrimmage yards were his first 100-yard game of the season, and his three touchdowns tied a career high. He scored twice in the first quarter , including a 36-yard run on the opening drive, and tied the game with a 1-yard plunge with 58 seconds left.

Tyjae Spears is out again Sunday with a knee injury, so Pollard should handle another heavy workload at Cincinnati. After that, the schedule turns hostile. A Week 9 bye leads into two games against Jacksonville in Weeks 10 and 12, and the Jaguars have been one of the league's stingiest defenses against running backs. Indianapolis and Pittsburgh, two other defenses that hold backs under the league average, visit Nashville in Weeks 15 and 17.

The Nov. 10 trade deadline adds another variable. ESPN's Dan Graziano reported Pollard is " more likely " to be moved than Colts star Jonathan Taylor, and the former Memphis back is in the final year of his contract. Still, NFL insider Ari Meirov reported the Titans have told teams they'd prefer to keep offensive contributors while they evaluate second-year quarterback Cam Ward. A trade could lift Pollard's price again, but a new team wouldn't guarantee him a lead role.

Ward hasn't thrown a touchdown pass in the first three quarters of any game this season, and rookie Carnell Tate led Tennessee with five catches for 69 yards against Cleveland. Tate is out Sunday with a shoulder injury, which could lower his asking price this week. If we're assuming a tough schedule is coming up for Pollard, maybe the Titans give Tate more looks, and he is someone you could try to acquire.

Last week: 5 rec., 103 yds, 1 TD on 12 tar., 35-21 L Rams

This week: at Jets, Sun., Nov. 1, 1 p.m. ET

Tucker leads Las Vegas with 474 receiving yards, and 200 of them came in the last two games. The Cincinnati product caught five passes for 97 yards and two touchdowns against Buffalo, then turned 12 targets into five catches, 103 yards and a 37-yard touchdown against the Rams. He has caught at least four passes in every game since Week 1.

The Week 7 line came with help from the scoreboard. Tucker was quiet against the Rams until Las Vegas fell behind by three scores in the fourth quarter, and the Raiders have lost four straight after a 3-0 start. Kirk Cousins is also getting Brock Bowers back to full strength. The star tight end practiced fully Thursday and Friday after a calf injury, and he has topped 70 receiving yards in all five of his games.

Sunday's trip to New York is a neutral matchup, but Seattle in Week 10 and the Chargers in Week 14 have been two of the toughest defenses for receivers lately. The Weeks 15 to 17 slate of Denver, Tennessee and Arizona looks neutral, so this sell rests more on how Tucker is producing than on the playoff schedule.

If the speedy receiver has been the borderline flex start that paid off the last two weeks, look for a replacement with a clearer path to consistent touches, like a running back with limited backfield competition.

Last week: 5 rec., 22 yds, 1 TD on 5 tar., 29-20 W 49ers

This week: at Buccaneers, Sun., Nov. 1, 1 p.m. ET

Pitts made our Week 7 sell-high list , and he scored again against San Francisco. The Florida product has four touchdowns in his last three games with exactly five catches in each, and he became the sixth-youngest tight end to reach 300 career receptions in the win over the 49ers.

The yardage hasn't kept pace with the scoring. Pitts has 124 receiving yards over that three-game stretch, including 22 yards on five catches last week, so touchdowns are carrying most of his fantasy output. Atlanta also leaned on all four tight ends against San Francisco. Pitts played 37 offensive snaps to Austin Hooper's 28 and Nick Muse's 21, and Muse caught a touchdown of his own.

He isn't the focal point of the offense, either. Bijan Robinson leads the NFL with 907 scrimmage yards, and Drake London has 616 receiving yards through seven games.

The schedule doesn't help the sell case. Kansas City in Week 10, Detroit in Week 13 and Washington in Week 15 have all been generous to tight ends, and Minnesota in Week 12 is the only clear problem. Instead, this comes down to track record. Pitts didn't top 8.0 PPR points in any of his first four games, and managers have sat through long stretches of uneven production from the former No. 4 overall pick over the years.

Most managers won't view the four-touchdown stretch as his new baseline, so you're hunting for the one who does. If that person even exists, maybe it's a Gators alumnus with a fond memory of the old days! Ask for a weekly starter at running back or receiver in return, assuming your other tight end is the more dependable option looking ahead.

articles.title: Mike Brown says the New York Knicks have something that 'the other 29 teams don't'
articles.summary: The New York Knicks head coach Mike Brown has hailed his team’s medical department amid all the injuries in the NBA lately. The number of injuries this early...
articles.body:
The New York Knicks head coach Mike Brown has hailed his team's medical department amid all the injuries in the NBA lately.

The number of injuries this early in the season has been remarkable, with several big names facing a spell on the sidelines already.

The Knicks, however, have been fortunate on the injury front, and Brown thinks he knows the real reason why.

Mike Brown says the New York Knicks' injury luck is down to three people

The New York Knicks have barely been affected by injuries this season.

Jose Alvarado is the only player who is currently sidelined, and according to CBS Sports, he could be back in the first week of November.

The same cannot be said about some of the other teams. Minnesota's Anthony Edwards, Indiana's Tyrese Haliburton, Oklahoma City's Chet Holmgren, Orlando's Paolo Banchero, and Portland's Ja Morant are all currently unavailable due to injuries.

When quizzed about the injury problems across the league this season, Brown attributed his side's luck to three staff members that no other team has: Quentin Dolan, Casey Smith and Anthony "Chico" Goenaga.

He said in his press conference, as per SNY Knicks: "Knock on wood. There are 30 teams, but there's only one Quentin Dolan. One Casey Smith. And one Chico.

"There is only one of those three people, and, knock on wood, the other 29 teams don't have them. So, I don't really care what the rest of them do."

Dolan works as Senior Vice President, Player Performance and Science Leader at the Knicks, advising on performance and science infrastructure, medical and conditioning and player availability.

Smith works as the Vice President of Sports Medicine, and his responsibilities include player health, medical care, performance optimisation and injury prevention for the roster.

Goenaga, popularly known as Chico, works as the Head Athletic Trainer and oversees the team's sports medicine, physical therapy, acute injury care and player rehabilitation programs.

articles.title: Travis Hunter Breaks Silence on Claims He Baited C.J. Stroud With ‘Fake Stumble’ Trick
articles.summary: Travis Hunter’s fourth-quarter interception of C.J. Stroud quickly became one of the most talked-about plays of the week. Social media users claimed Hunter o...
articles.body:
Travis Hunter's fourth-quarter interception of C.J. Stroud quickly became one of the most talked-about plays of the week. Social media users claimed Hunter once explained a "fake stumble" trick while at Colorado.

Travis Hunter now is getting the allegation that he used his old trick in the fourth-quarter interception of C.J. Stroud.

Travis Hunter responds to "fake stumble" allegation

In the fourth quarter of the Jacksonville Jaguars ' game against the Houston Texans , Travis Hunter made a game-changing defensive play. Houston led 31-28 after Hunter himself had scored a 7-yard touchdown reception earlier in the period. On the Texans' next drive, a 12-play, 63-yard march that pushed deep into Jacksonville territory, C.J. Stroud threw a pass toward the end zone with 3:59 remaining. Hunter, lining up at cornerback, broke on the ball and intercepted it.

Some viewers claimed Hunter appeared to briefly lower his body and lean off-balance just before reacting, which fueled speculation that he had intentionally baited Stroud. Hunter addressed the rumors directly in a press conference. He flatly denied ever describing or using such a technique.

"No, I've never said that. I don't know. They just be making up stuff. I've never said that. Nobody wants to stumble and try to make it look like something it's not. My coach told me to burn, so I felt like I was me. I put my eyes down and got to the minute as fast as I can." Hunter said.

Analysts and fans piled on, with some calling the technique "genius" and suggesting other defensive backs should copy it.

Social media were quick to build a narrative. "Genius: Travis Hunter revealed that he does a fake stumble to trick QBs into throwing his way, and CJ Stroud immediately fell for it." NFL insider Dov Kleiman posted .

The Football Forever account added more detail. "While at Colorado, Travis Hunter explained how he 'fake stumbles' to trick QBs into throwing the ball – he says he intentionally squats low and leans over, looking off-center to make it seem like he tripped or got caught slipping, a method he used to intercept C.J. Stroud," it wrote .

These claims linked the interception to comments Hunter supposedly made during his college career at Colorado. Analysts and fans piled on, with some calling the technique "genius" and suggesting other defensive backs should copy it. One podcast host described the play as one of the "craziest" he had ever seen, claiming Hunter pretended to slip and looked away to bait the throw.

articles.body: La cuarta edición de los Juegos de la Juventud serán inaugurados oficialmente este 31 de octubre. Dakar, capital de Senegal, acoge una competición que debía haberse disputado en 2022, pero quedó aplazada por la pandemia. Un total de 2.700 jóvenes de todo 87 países se dan cita en busca de alguna de las medallas que pondrán en liza las 151 pruebas del programa deportivo. La competición arrancó ya en el béisbol 5, remo de mar y vóley playa. Estos Juegos se han convertido en un escaparate para disciplinas que aspiran a formar parte del programa olímpico. Dakar será el escenario del estreno del wushu, que reunirá a 48 deportistas de 47 comités olímpicos nacionales entre el 1 y el 3 de noviembre. La competición se centrará en el taolu, una modalidad que combina rutinas de ataque y defensa con movimientos acrobáticos, ejercicios de equilibrio y demostraciones de velocidad y precisión. El programa está compuesto por cuatro pruebas, dos masculinas y dos femeninas. Los participantes competirán en changquan combinado, una modalidad que integra rutinas de puño largo y bastón (gunshu), y taijiquan combinado, que combina movimientos fluidos y controlados con el manejo del abanico (taijishan). Cada prueba reunirá a 12 deportistas, de los que los ocho mejores lograrán el billete para la final. La presencia del wushu en estos Juegos era una aspiración que se marcó la Federación Internacional desde su fundación en 1990. Y puede ser el primer paso para que llegue a ser olímpico. No es una pretensión descabellada, viendo el camino que recorrieron antes otros deportes hasta ser incluidos en el programa del evento multideportivo por excelencia. "Tengo muchas ganas de ir a ver el wushu y aprender más sobre él. Sé que es un deporte muy importante para China, pero también para muchos otros países del mundo", comentó Kirsty Coventry, presidenta del COI, en la rueda de prensa previa al inicio de estos Juegos. En ella también recordó que esta cita da a conocer nuevos deportes al público. El baloncesto 3x3 se estrenó en la primera edición de los Juegos de la Juventud, en Singapur 2010. En Tokio 2020 debutó en los Juegos Olímpicos. La escalada se probó en el programa de la edición de Buenos Aires 2018 cuando dos años antes ya se había incluido en el programa deportivo de Tokio 2020. Lo mismo pasó con el rugby 7. Con su presencia ya aprobada para Río 2016, se disputó antes en los Juegos de la Juventud de Nankín 2014. La capital argentina también acogió el breakdance que fue olímpico en París 2024. No ha corrido la misma suerte, de momento, otros deportes como el fútbol sala, el balonmano playa, el patinaje de velocidad sobre ruedas o el baile deportivo.

articles.title: West Indies thrash Bangladesh by eight wickets in first Test in Mirpur
articles.summary: West Indies extended ‌their encouraging run in red-ball cricket with an emphatic eight-wicket victory ⁠over Bangladesh.
articles.body:
Brandon King struck a career-best 81 not out as West Indies cruised to an eight-wicket win over Bangladesh in the first Test on Saturday to take a 1-0 lead in the two-match series.

King hit 10 fours and a six in his 115-ball knock to help the visitors chase down the target of 170 in 35.1 overs on the fourth day in Mirpur after Bangladesh were bowled out for 142 in their second innings.

Jomel Warrican, named player of the match, claimed 4-63 to follow up his five-wicket haul in Bangladesh’s first innings as the hosts were bowled out in 48.4 overs.

West Indies captain Roston Chase took 5-36 in the second innings , his fifth five-wicket haul in Test cricket.

Chase said the team was determined to win the series and go up in the rankings.

“The guys were determined, even though we didn’t have a good start in the first innings,” Chase said.

“We lost the lead, but we were still determined to fight back and try to win the game, and that’s what we did.”

Bangladesh had resumed the fourth day at 79-6, holding a lead of 106, but their hopes of setting a challenging target suffered an early blow when Jaker Ali edged Warrican to slip, where Chase took the catch.

Jaker, who scored 22 off 34 balls, was the second-highest scorer for Bangladesh in the innings.

Nayeem Hasan survived two dropped catches off Chase, on 21 and 29, to keep Bangladesh going.

Nayeem added 26 runs with Hasan Mahmud before Warrican trapped the latter lbw for eight.

Taijul Islam contributed eight in a 17-run partnership with Nayeem before Chase dismissed him to leave Bangladesh at 127-9.

Nayeem then reached his maiden Test half-century off 87 balls, with four boundaries, but his resistance ended when he attempted to hit Chase over long-on and was caught by Joshua Bishop.

He made 52 off 91 balls, while Shoriful Islam remained unbeaten on seven as Bangladesh were dismissed cheaply.

Bangladesh skipper Najmul Hossain Shanto said his team failed to execute their plans.

“All three departments didn’t do well, especially in the field. These things can happen sometimes, but I believe the intention and preparation were quite good,” he said.

“Going forward, we need to look at those areas and work out how we can do better in these conditions.”

West Indies started confidently, with openers King and John Campbell continuing their aggressive approach to take the visitors to 64 without loss in 14.1 overs before rain interrupted play.

After a delay of about an hour, they added another 23 runs before bad light and lightning forced a further stoppage of 45 minutes.

King was dropped on 70 by substitute fielder Ebadot Hossain off Taijul after the break, but the opener made Bangladesh pay with his fine, unbeaten knock.

Campbell fell just short of a half-century, bowled by Shoriful for 49 off 55 balls, with six fours and a six.

The victory continued a positive period for West Indies, who recently pushed India in a one-day series and shared a 2-2 draw ‌in ‌a T20 series against the world champions earlier this month.

The second Test will be played in Sylhet from November 5.

articles.title: B/R's Favorite 10 NHL Goalie Masks of All Time
articles.summary: While Jason Voorhees made the goalie mask something to fear, goalies across the NHL have made it their palette for creativity and intimidation for opponents for decades. Of the hundreds, if not thousands, of different masks over the years, many of them set themselves apart from the pack by becoming iconic.
articles.body:
While Jason Voorhees made the goalie mask something to fear, goalies across the NHL have made it their palette for creativity and intimidation for opponents for decades. Of the hundreds, if not thousands, of different masks over the years, many of them set themselves apart from the pack by becoming iconic.

Whether it's the beauty of the art, the iconography included, or the grim reality, masks have given goalies a chance to make their personalities seen by everyone. Picking out our favorites from the time Jacques Plante started wearing a mask full-time in 1959 until now has made for a lot of fun remembering guys and thinking back on what they wore during their careers.

We've assembled a gallery of our favorite masks all-time, and although we're not ranking them, we are appreciating the players and their artists who made these classic looks possible all the same.

There's arguably no mask more famous than the "face-hugger" mask worn by Bruins goalie Gerry Cheevers.

Cheevers' mask was painted with stitch marks where he would've been cut by pucks that went off it. While goalies were using masks in the early 70s, Cheevers was one of the first to have his painted up, and what a way to do it. His style set a bar that's been hard for most to reach when it comes to art and intimidation.

Not only were the stitches off-putting, but they also served as a reminder to opponents that, yes, he will stop the puck at any cost, whether it's with the pads, trapper, or even his face if necessary. Cheevers' mask goes real hard and remains the gold standard to this day.

The 80s and 90s helped establish so many classic goalie mask looks that left a legacy, and Mike Richter's "Lady Liberty" mask was one of those.

Richter helping lead the New York Rangers to their first Stanley Cup in 54 years in 1994 helped make all of those players household names to a degree, and Richter being an American and leading New York City's team to a Cup made him a celebrity, and his mask embodied everything about the Rangers, New York, and ultimately the United States as well.

After all, Richter was the goalie for Team USA at the 1996 World Cup of Hockey, which won gold as well, and did so donning the same mask. Richter wore this mask throughout his career, and his big-game legacy became attached to that look. Even Henrik Lundqvist paid homage to Richter and his mask during his own incredible career with the Rangers.

Ken Dryden was one of the great gentlemen of hockey, and he was also a goalie with an iconic mask as well.

Dryden's "bullseye" mask became iconic while he and the Canadiens stomped across the NHL during his career. It would've been wrong for a team as good as the Habs not to have a goalie with a legendary look, and Dryden's bleu, blanc et rouge mask more than accomplished that.

Dryden's legacy in Montréal is so pronounced, and he was so beloved and respected that upon his passing, the Canadiens paid tribute to him in a simple, yet beautiful way by displaying his mask atop the goal with a spotlight on the net during the 2025 home opener on Oct. 14, 2025.

Although Gary Bromley may not be the most famous NHL goalie, the guy they called "Bones" because of his slight build used that nickname to create an incredible look for his mask.

Bromley's skull-face mask is the kind of thing you'd expect in a horror movie or a bank heist. Instead, he wore it to stop pucks during his time with Vancouver in the late 70s-early 80s.

The ultra-realistic looking skull is as hardcore looking as anything we've ever seen on a goalie mask and while modern masks don't lend themselves well to this sort of artwork, masks of those days didn't go hard like this either. The "Bones" mask is as good as it gets for any kind of mask.

One goalie who set the tone immediately upon arriving in the NHL with their play and their mask art was Felix Potvin.

"The Cat" had the kind of play that inspired Leafs teammates and fans alike, and his classic mask art was both ultra cool and ferocious. The animalistic style of the art stood out, and the design he used in Toronto was one he kept throughout his career in Long Island, Los Angeles, Vancouver, and Boston, albeit with those teams' colors instead.

Potvin's style was uniquely his, and when he debuted it in Toronto, it created a look that stayed with him for good.

When you've got a nickname like "CuJo," coming up with a great mask idea isn't all that difficult. After all, when you've got an evil dog from a Stephen King book to set the tone, the rest is gravy, and for Curtis Joseph, adopting that design became his own legacy.

Throughout Joseph's career, from St. Louis to Edmonton to Toronto to Detroit, Phoenix, and Calgary alike, the snarling beast adorned his mask in the various team colors to go with it. We threw it back to his St. Louis mask because that's where it all began, but his Toronto mask is worth noting as well for its ferocity.

Sometimes a goalie mask is cool because of the greatness attached to the player, and Martin Brodeur helped make his mask iconic by simply being one of the best of a generation.

Brodeur's Devils legacy is untouchable. Three Stanley Cups, four Vezinas, and, of course, a spot in the Hall of Fame — all of it done with his particular style, the Devils mask on his head.

The red, black, and white mask to go with the Devils' colors made it known your team was in for a long night, even if you got through New Jersey's defense to get to the net, all because Brodeur was there waiting to stop you in the end.

In his time with the Edmonton Oilers, Grant Fuhr helped them win multiple Stanley Cups. He also helped set the standard for incredibly cool masks.

Fuhr wore numerous styles of masks in his time with the Oilers, but the one we remember best featured the orange oil drop below the cage and a wild blue, orange, and white flurry of design on the rest of the mask.

When a look helps win Cups, it gets to be popular, but Fuhr's style and cool-under-fire approach to the position helped out, too. We could've picked any number of Fuhr's other masks from his career in St. Louis, Toronto, Buffalo, and Los Angeles, but his Oilers masks set the bar.

What Gary Bromley's skull mask started in the 80s, Miikka Kiprusoff's mask with the Calgary Flames was made into art.

Kiprusoff's screeching skull mask is truly something else, with the skulls on each side of the helmet, as well as the face of a skull with glaring eyes on its chin. Yes, it's got his nickname and number on it, but would you even notice it without having it pointed out? The skulls demand your attention.

Kipper's mask was really one of a kind in that it leaned into such a heavy metal-like style and yet made it so incredibly cool.

You could argue that there's no movie scarier than "Jaws," and you could also argue there's no goalie mask scarier than the one Brian Hayward wore during his time with the San Jose Sharks.

Hayward's shark head mask that featured his face in the open mouth of a great white shark, teeth and all, is truly one of a kind. The mask's art is simply a shark opening wide like you'd see in "Jaws," and its realistic appearance is so incredible it's a wonder we haven't seen more mask art inspired by it.

Hayward was with the Sharks at their inception, and having a mask done up just like "Jaws" made all the sense in the world. You could argue his mask helped give the new team even more attention just by being one of the coolest things anyone's seen in a long time.

articles.title: Gemma Triay y Delfi Brea conquistan el Kuwait Major y dan un golpe al número uno
articles.standfirst: Remontan ante Ari Sánchez y Andrea Ustero (3-6, 6-1 y 6-1) y prácticamente sentencian el número uno
articles.summary: Remontan ante Ari Sánchez y Andrea Ustero (3-6, 6-1 y 6-1) y prácticamente sentencian el número uno
articles.body: El trono no se entrega sin resistencia, pero en Kuwait volvió a tener las mismas dueñas. Gemma Triay y Delfi Brea conquistaron el segundo Major de la temporada después de remontar a Ari Sánchez y Andrea Ustero por 3-6, 6-1 y 6-1. Las número uno necesitaron un set para encontrar su sitio, pero cuando lo hicieron desplegaron toda su autoridad para darle la vuelta a una final que había comenzado cuesta arriba. Casi dos meses después de su último título, conquistado durante la primera semana de septiembre en Madrid, la pareja hispanoargentina vuelve a levantar un trofeo. Es el séptimo de su temporada, el segundo Major y, sobre todo, un golpe de autoridad en la carrera por terminar el año en lo más alto de la Race. La final comenzó con Ari Sánchez y Andrea Ustero dispuestas a prolongar su extraordinario momento de forma. Las catalanas saltaron a la pista con una marcha más y dibujaron un prometedor 3-0 que obligó a Gemma y Delfi a reaccionar. Las número uno fueron entrando poco a poco en calor, ajustaron sus posiciones y comenzaron a encontrar mejores sensaciones hasta devolver la igualdad al marcador. El 3-3 anunciaba que la final recuperaba el equilibrio, pero Ari y Andrea todavía tenían algo que decir. Un nuevo break les permitió tomar ventaja y, esta vez, no dejaron escapar la oportunidad. Con el 6-3 cerraron el primer capítulo y se adelantaron en una final que empezaba a exigir respuestas a las grandes favoritas. Y la respuesta llegó con contundencia. Gemma y Delfi elevaron su nivel, ganaron presencia en la pista y comenzaron a imponer un ritmo que sus rivales ya no conseguían seguir. El break en el cuarto juego abrió una brecha que las número uno se encargaron de ampliar hasta el 4-1. Ari y Andrea empezaron a perder precisión, mientras las campeonas encontraban cada vez más espacios para hacer daño. Una doble falta de Sánchez en un momento delicado terminó facilitando otro break que colocó el 5-1 en el marcador. Con el servicio a favor, Gemma y Delfi no perdonaron y cerraron la manga por 6-1. La final quedaba igualada, pero las sensaciones habían cambiado por completo. El tercer set fue la confirmación de que las número uno habían encontrado definitivamente el camino. Un break inicial las puso por delante y, desde ese momento, las reinas del pádel jugaron con una seguridad que fue desarmando poco a poco a sus rivales. Ari Sánchez, lejos de las sensaciones del primer parcial, se mostró errática, sin ritmo y sin el control que acostumbra a imponer sobre la pista. Andrea tampoco conseguía encontrar continuidad ante unas Gemma y Delfi cada vez más sólidas, con menos errores y una lectura impecable de los intercambios. El segundo break llevó el marcador hasta el 4-1 y terminó de inclinar una final en la que las campeonas ya no concedían prácticamente nada. El 6-1 definitivo certificó una remontada incontestable y devolvió a Gemma y Delfi a lo más alto del podio. El título tiene también una dimensión histórica para Gemma Triay. La menorquina alcanza los 59 títulos en su carrera y supera los 58 que compartía hasta ahora con Ale Salazar y Ari Sánchez, convirtiéndose en la jugadora con más trofeos desde la era PPT. Un registro que habla de longevidad, talento y una capacidad extraordinaria para mantenerse en la élite a través de distintas generaciones y compañeras. En Kuwait, además, ha vuelto a demostrar que sigue teniendo hambre de historia. Ari Sánchez y Andrea Ustero habían llegado a Kuwait con la oportunidad de acercarse todavía más a la cima, pero Gemma y Delfi han sabido defender su territorio en el momento decisivo. La Race sigue teniendo a las mismas líderes y ahora con un argumento de peso añadido: las número uno han respondido cuando más presión había, ante sus perseguidoras directas y en una final de Major. Después de casi dos meses sin levantar un trofeo, han vuelto a reinar. Y lo han hecho con la autoridad de quienes no están dispuestas a ceder la corona.

articles.title: South Africa hammer Australia as Harmer takes career best bowling of 6-16
articles.summary: Simon Harmer picked a career-best 6-16 as South Africa beat Australia by 176 runs to clinch Test series 2-1.
articles.body:
Australia ‌captain Pat Cummins said it was fair to ask questions about his side after they ⁠slipped to two heavy ⁠defeats in a row against hosts South Africa to lose the three-match series 2-1 at Newlands on Saturday.

Set 288 for victory, Australia were rocked early on and could ⁠manage only 111 to lose the third Test by 176 runs, following their defeat by an innings and 31 runs in the second match in the series.

Australia next host New Zealand, and Cummins ⁠said the series loss meant questions were inevitable as South Africa took over from them as the number one side in the Test world rankings.

“We lost two games in a row. I think it’s fair to be asking questions and we’ll be asking them internally as well,” Cummins told reporters. “We are a very good ‌side, but I think we need to get a little bit better if we want to get back to number one [in the world].

“Maybe that’s a change of style, maybe it’s a change of personnel in some instances. We’ll work it out.”

Cummins made the surprise decision to bowl first after winning the toss on the first morning, something that had been done only 11 times before in Tests at Newlands since 1889.

As it proved, batting last was difficult on a wearing ⁠surface, and Australia fell to the spin of Simon Harmer, who took ⁠career-best figures of 10-120 in the match.

“We knew it was going to be a high-scoring game,” Cummins said. “We probably thought it was going to do a little bit more on day one than it did.

“You don’t win the toss and think you’re ⁠going to bowl the opposition out for 100 or 200, but we thought we could get 10 wickets on day one and that would ⁠put us right ahead of the game.”

Cummins said poor decisions cost ⁠his batters and that their chase was as good as over in the first half-hour of the day.

“Chasing 280-odd was never going to be easy, but we all turned up today and saw a pretty clear path forward. I thought it was ‌achievable, but we never really gave ourselves a chance,” he said.

“There were a few really poor decisions. I know it’s a day-five wicket, but I don’t think it was drastic. There were runs to ‌be ‌scored out there; there were lots of balls to face.

“I think there are a few decisions the boys would like back. We have to get better. It’s happened a few times now.”

articles.title: India make history, beat Uganda to win inaugural Women’s Commonwealth Kabaddi Championship
articles.summary: India made history by defeating Uganda 35-15 in the final to win the inaugural women’s Commonwealth Kabaddi Championship in Ahmedabad on Saturday.
articles.body: India made history by defeating Uganda 35-15 in the final to win the inaugural women’s Commonwealth Kabaddi Championship in Ahmedabad on Saturday. Led by captain Nidhi Sharma, the team completed a perfect campaign, winning all six matches without a defeat to lift the trophy.Sakshi was India’s top scorer in the final, collecting nine raid points from 10 attempts, including two bonus points. She scored seven points in the first half alone. Anu contributed six raid points, while captain Nidhi added five.Defenders Ritu and Suman also played a key role, earning four tackle points each.India started strongly and led 7-3 with 10 minutes left in the first half. They then increased the pressure, scoring 15 points against Uganda’s four to take a commanding 22-7 lead at the break. India’s raiders remained successful throughout the first half, while Uganda struggled to stop them.Uganda put up a better fight after the break, scoring seven raid points compared to India’s six. However, India’s second All-Out with less than 10 minutes remaining made the result almost certain.Nakayongo Shirat was Uganda’s best performer with 11 points, but her efforts were not enough to challenge India.Sakshi praises team effortAfter the win, Sakshi expressed her happiness and spoke about the importance of the tournament for the sport.She said, “I’m feeling great that I could score 9 raid points and help the team win. The atmosphere in the team is euphoric after winning the gold medal, and everyone is very happy. This event was very important for Kabaddi, as such International tournaments will help the growth of the sport, and our young players will benefit a lot from this experience."I could see a lot of improvement in other teams from last year. I want to thank AKFI for organising such a wonderful championship.”Sakshi finished the tournament with 52 points in six matches and was named India’s standout performer in the final.India began their campaign with a 73-13 win over Malaysia and went on to beat Singapore, Uganda and Nigeria in the group stage.They then defeated Sri Lanka in the semifinal before beating Uganda in the final to become the first women’s champions of the competition.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates.
