articles.title: 8 Trade Ideas for Nikita Kucherov Amid NHL Rumors
articles.summary: NHL fans have become hardened to big names requesting trades, but Nikita Kucherov's October Surprise breaks into new territory.
articles.body:
NHL fans have become hardened to big names requesting trades, but Nikita Kucherov's October Surprise breaks into new territory.

This is not a young player looking to head closer to home, or a franchise icon disillusioned with losing. Kucherov is the Lightning's all-time point leader. He's won two Stanley Cups in Tampa.

Even if there were some questions about whether he'd look elsewhere in free agency this July, I don't think anyone anticipated a demand from his own camp to leave the team.

Lightning management is pushing back publicly, but we've all seen how quickly those walls can come down once a trade demand creates a media circus and sinks the locker room. Just ask Ottawa, Vancouver, or Detroit.

So we'll see if the Lightning can put this toothpaste back in the tube. If not, we're approaching new territory on the trade market. One has to wonder, also, if Tampa tries to salvage this by spinning assets from a Kucherov trade into a different big move. Dylan Larkin, anyone?

Given his demands for a massive contract and reportedly a desire to play with a " superstar ," according to ESPN's Emily Kaplan, let's look at what teams may be a match for a Nikita Kucherov trade.

The Fit: The Canadiens have been big-fish hunting (Kirill Marchenko, Dylan Larkin) in the last 6 months. Tidy work locking up Lane Hutson, Ivan Demidov, Nick Suzuki, and Juraj Slafkovsky well below their actual value means that they can afford to throw a big number at a player like Kucherov. The Habs are pretty strong on the wing and need a center more than anything else, but talent is talent, and Kucherov would put them into a new tier of contention.

Notable Trade Pieces: In a world where Kucherov is going to the highest bidder, Montreal has the pieces to keep up. At the NHL level, their most attractive piece may be defenseman Kaiden Guhle. He's a strong skater and a physical shutdown defenseman, but the Habs have Hutson and Matheson on the left side.

Tampa's starting demand may be prospect Michael Hage. The 20-year-old center has been dominant at the University of Michigan. He's a skilled offensive center who makes plays at NHL speed. Montreal will hesitate to move someone all but penciled in as a future top-six center, but we're talking about Kucherov.

Another name that would come up is 19-year-old KHL breakout star Alexander Zharovsky, who was nearly sent to Toronto for Matthew Knies at the last trade deadline. Defenseman David Reinbacher would also be a natural secondary piece in a monumental trade like this.

The Fit: This really depends on Kucherov's priorities. If he's looking to immediately contend and partner with other superstars, Seattle won't make sense. If he's looking to land the biggest paycheck possible, then the Kraken may be the optimal landing spot. They haven't had a true star player since they were created in 2021, and they attempted to throw a bonkers amount of money at Jason Robertson and Artemi Panarin.

How desperate is Seattle? They could make as compelling an offer as anyone if GM Jason Botterill puts Berkly Catton or Matty Beniers on the table. That seems unlikely, but again, the Kraken are more determined than any other team to add a player like Kucherov.

More realistically, we're looking at some impact players with lesser stature. Center Shane Wright is the obvious starting point. They've been trying to find a trade for him. The 22-year-old is already a strong defensive center who hit 44 points in his first full NHL season. Tampa needs a strong third-line center, and he'd step in as exactly that, with room to grow into top-six performances.

If Tampa wants a replacement winger, I'd wonder about Kaapo Kakko. Of course, he has not lived up to pre-draft hype and is well off the standard of Kucherov, but Kakko is still just 25, plays like a top-six winger, and is finally finding some offense; he has 51 points in his last 79 NHL games.

Prospect Jake O'Brien is also a candidate to move. The former eighth-overall pick is a creative, skilled player who has top-six upside at just 19 years old.

The Fit: The Hurricanes were a buzzsaw last season and won the Stanley Cup. Ironically, the feeling inside the organization is that the team was not in its final form. Management has been carefully curating financial flexibility and trade assets, hoping to land a superstar. They tried with Mikko Rantanen but had to pivot. They'd like to try again.

Tampa Bay, to any extent it wishes to move Kucherov, would probably vomit at the thought of sending him to a conference rival. They may have no choice, depending on how this plays out.

The Hurricanes have a lot to offer, and it really depends on what direction Tampa Bay wants to go. The relationship with Andrei Svechnikov has been turbulent, though they pushed through last season, and he made an impact at critical moments. But if Carolina were to make him available, it's tough to see any team putting a better player on the table.

I'd wonder about Jackson Blake. Carolina would not love the idea, but it's Nikita Kucherov.

Carolina also has a couple of top prospects in Bradly Nadeau and Felix Unger-Sorum. Winger Nadeau in particular has excelled in the AHL and is a pure scorer with 30-goal upside in the NHL. The Hurricanes have struggled to find a full-time position for him with the big club, and they'd be willing to move him for an impact player even below the standard of Kucherov.

Winners and Losers From NHL's 1st Month 📊

The Fit: The Bruins are fairly pleased with their teamwide process, but they've been frustrated by the lack of goals over the last few seasons. It's been better this season, though the power play is still average, and Morgan Geekie has just one goal in 14 games.

Tampa Bay will rue yet another division rival entering this discussion, and Boston may have to knock their socks off.

It's not good form to trade a guy months after you trade two first-round picks for his services, but I struggle to see Boston's path to Kucherov without offering JJ Peterka. The German winger is speedy and finishes off the rush. He's just 24 years old and looks to be a 50-70 point winger depending on how streaky he is and whether the systems are built for his play. Would the Bruins be willing to get older in order to make a massive upgrade?

Tampa would absolutely ask about James Hagens, and the Bruins would make that a non-starter. Prospect Dean Letourneau would have to be included, though. The 6'7" center is a bit of a project, but he started to connect the dots last season and was above a point-per-game pace at Boston College. He is very skilled for his size and has a lethal shot.

The Fit: The Blackhawks are in year four of the Connor Bedard era and have barely improved. At some point, he's going to get fed up. More pointedly, they have utterly failed to provide him with legitimate offensive help. You could draw names from a hat and likely come up with better options than Tyler Bertuzzi or a dilapidated Patrick Kane. The Blackhawks have a lot of young assets. Too many. They'd like to package some for a difference-maker.

If Tampa is forced to trade Kucherov, they'd prefer to do so to a Western Conference team that isn't an immediate Cup threat like Chicago.

Notable Trade Pieces: Teuvo Teravainen could step into a second-line role in Tampa Bay. He's miles off Kucherov's talent, but he's a smart two-way winger who becomes a UFA in 2027.

The meat of a Blackhawks offer would be in its top young talent. Oliver Moore and Frank Nazar are both high-octane centers who project for a middle-six role in the NHL. Nazar competes hard and gets to the net. Moore has electric speed and solid playmaking instincts.

The Blackhawks also have a bevvy of prospects from which to pull. Wingers Roman Kantserov, Nick Lardis, and Vaclav Nestrasil all have top-six upside. Plus, Chicago's first-round picks project to be better than those of most other teams that may be involved in this sweepstakes.

The Fit: The Mammoth are one of the teams that have been big-game hunting. They went after Connor Hellebuyck and have been linked to Dylan Larkin. It's a very good team that is one top player away from ascending into a great team. Utah has their young guys locked up long-term, and they have a lot of money coming off the books this summer at forward.

They have the financial wiggle room and the assets to go after a player like Kucherov. If he is willing to head there. Kucherov is reportedly looking to link up with a "superstar." Logan Cooley and Dylan Guenther are excellent players, but you need to stretch the definition to fit them in.

Notable Trade Pieces: A trade may be more futures-based than Tampa Bay would wish for, but Utah has high-end talent on the precipice of making a difference in the NHL.

Tij Iginla would absolutely surface in these discussions. The son of NHL superstar Jarome is a former sixth-overall pick. He was dominant in the WHL (when healthy) and scored a lot of goals thanks to his energy, polished, powerful footwork, and a heavy shot.

Daniil But is a 6'5" winger with a fantastic ability to maneuver with the puck. He's already shown flashes in the NHL.

The toughest part is finding an established NHLer to swap. Barrett Hayton would make sense, but New Jersey's offer sheet over the summer means Utah can't trade him. Lawson Crouse is a decent middle-six winger but doesn't measure up to others that competing teams might offer, and he's a UFA in July.

The Fit: The Flyers viewed themselves as a competitive, well-functioning team that could take the next step with an infusion of talent at the top of the roster. That merited the offer sheet to Leo Carlsson over the summer.

Their belief in the team as currently constructed has been challenged by an atrocious start to the 2026-27 season, but that may only feed their desire to add an impact offensive player. Is Kucherov willing to join a work-in-progress? We know the Flyers will pay a high salary, and he'd be the ideal mentor for Matvei Michkov.

Travis Konecny is a top-six NHL winger who has consistently hit 65-70 points in the last few NHL seasons. He battles hard but has enough offensive touch. However, his name was floated as one player whom the Flyers were "frustrated" with during a winless start to the season.

The Flyers have some interesting prospects, though none who would stand out compared to what other teams may offer. We can assume that Porter Martone, and Michkov aren't available. Jett Luchanko has plateaued in his development, but he has the makeup that a coach like Jon Cooper often finds a way to maximize. He could be a great third-line center option for Tampa by next season.

Denver Barkey would be a perfect fit for Tampa Bay's bottom-six and would be a fun sweetener to throw in the deal.

The Fit: Well, let's start with the reasons there isn't a fit in Manhattan. The Rangers are white-knuckling it through the season without Igor Shesterkin and are in serious danger of missing the playoffs for a third straight season. They already have a few long-term contracts for aging players on the books. The biggest need in the organization, without question, is a first-line center. Big money is already invested on the wing in Pavel Dorofeyev and Alexis Lafrenière, plus more to come with Gabe Perreault. They have already traded away two first-round picks in the next four seasons, and the prospect pool is average.

On the other hand, they are desperate. Whether justified or not, the mandate is to compete now. The offense is stagnant, and Tye Kartye is not a legitimate top-six wing option. The Rangers have historically made moves like this in turbulent circumstances. For all their flaws, they certainly have superstars in Adam Fox and Igor Shesterkin. Igor Shesterkin, Dorofeyev, and Vladislav Gavrikov may bring a desirable social factor for the Russian winger.

Tampa Bay would ask about Lafrenière and Perreault. Hopefully, GM Chris Drury would make them non-starters. Will Cuylle would make more sense. A good player who hits and will chip in 20-25 goals, but he is limited creatively and is ideally a third-liner on a contender. He's up for an extension this summer, and the Rangers have other priorities.

Braden Schneider's inclusion would make sense. The Rangers do not have him in their long-term plans, and Tampa's coaching staff has worked wonders with defensemen like him who have the physical tools and a willingness to learn but haven't fully figured it out in other places.

The Rangers also have a lot of B-tier prospects whom Tampa Bay might like. Wingers Liam Greentree and Malcolm Spence have good physical profiles and have high odds of NHL careers, while EJ Emery is another defenseman with an excellent physical profile but needs some hands-on coaching to reach his second-pairing upside.

articles.title: Pakistan beat Sri Lanka as Zaman’s century turns thrilling tri-series final
articles.summary: Fakhar Zaman’s century outdoes Kamindu Mendis and propels Pakistan to three-wicket win against Sri Lanka in cricket final.
articles.body:
Opener Fakhar Zaman overcame a bruised knee and a lean spell to score 127 to help Pakistan beat Sri Lanka by three wickets in the final of the one-day international cricket tri-series on Saturday.

Zaman’s entertaining innings and Arafat Minhas’s robust 61 off 31 balls took Pakistan to a winning 331-7 in 48.3 overs, as the Sri Lankan bowlers found it hard to control the wet ball because of dew in Lahore.

Earlier, Kamindu Mendis’ 131, his maiden ODI century, propelled Sri Lanka to 325-8 while batting first for the first time in the tournament.

Zaman came into the final with only 31 runs in his last four innings and spent most of the time in the dressing room after injuring his right knee while fielding.

Pakistan lost Maaz Sadaqat for 5 and Babar Azam for a five-ball duck, much to the disappointment of the 31,265 home fans at Gaddafi Stadium, but Zaman revived the chase with 19-year-old Saad Baig, who made 74 off 75 balls. They put up a 149-run stand.

Sri Lanka’s Maheesh Theekshana, playing his first match in the tri-series, missed out on claiming Zaman on 69 and 106, when he couldn’t hold on to a return catch. Theekshana dropped Zaman again, a sitter on the boundary, after reaching his century off 84 balls.

Zaman’s 99-ball knock finally ended in the 34th over when he was clean bowled by Dilshan Madushanka with Pakistan still 106 runs from victory. Madushanka took 3-63.

The wet ball couldn’t help Sri Lanka as the young pair of Minhas and Hasan Nawaz (37 not out) kept their nerve before Asitha Fernando (2-72) added to the drama by bagging the wickets of Minhas and Faheem Ashraf off successive balls.

The other tri-series team, England, was knocked out after losing three of its four games.

articles.title: Do Brewers Need To Trade One Of Their Young Outfielders After World Series Win?
articles.summary: The Milwaukee Brewers may have an outfield logjam
articles.body:
The Milwaukee Brewers have four very talented outfielders under club control for years to come, but may need to consider trading one of them.

Jackson Chourio, Garrett Mitchell, Sal Frelick and Luis Lara were integral to the Brewers winning it all, but unfortunately, not all of them can play every day. In 2025, Frelick hit .280 and played pretty much every game. This year, he played through a torn labrum and will likely need surgery after the season.

He hit .230 this year, but is a premium defender and recorded a hit in all but two of the 10 postseason games he played in. He hit a huge home run in Game 2 of the World Series and is a huge part of the clubhouse. He is under club control through 2029.

Mitchell played in his first full season this year and was great for the Brewers. He played every day and posted a .771 OPS while playing elite defense. He is under club control through 2028.

Chourio is one of the best players in baseball and has already signed an extension that keeps him under team control through 2033.

Lara signed an extension this year before even making his debut. He is an amazing defender and platooned with Frelick in right field. He is a switch-hitter, and the Brewers believe he can be a great offensive player.

For the time being, all four can coexist, with Frelick and Lara sharing right field. However, if the team re-signs Jake Bauers, there will be a decision to be made.

Bauers is nowhere near the defender that Lara and Frelick are, but he is a far better hitter. This season, he played right field at times so the Brewers could get him and Andrew Vaughn, who is also a great hitter, in the lineup together. If the Brewers pay Bauers, there's no way he won't play every game.

The decision the team needs to make is whether to trade Mitchell or Frelick, or to trade Vaughn if they re-sign Bauers.

If the team believes Frelick can be the hitter he was in 2025, they would be foolish to trade him. Mitchell has the potential to be an All-Star-caliber player, so trading him may also be a miscalculation.

The Brewers don't need to trade any of their outfielders right now, and Frelick platooning with Lara is a likely scenario going into next season. However, if Bauers does end up staying in Milwaukee, something will have to be done. Vaughn is too good a hitter to be sitting on the bench.

articles.title: Purdue football down two starters, including captain, at Penn State
articles.summary: After getting good news on two former starters this week, Purdue football will be down two others at Penn State, including an offensive captain.

UNIVERSITY PARK, Pennsylvania − The injury big giveth and it taketh away for Purdue football ahead of Saturday's kickoff at Penn State .

The Boilermakers could be without two starters against the Nittany Lions , the same week where they return two others from a long hiatus.

Receiver and captain De'Nylon Morrissette, along with safety Jaden Mangham, will not play.

Morrissette has 8 catches for 125 yards and a touchdown this season after sitting out all of 2025 after tightrope surgery to repair multiple torn ligaments in his ankle. Mangham has 30 tackles and a pass breakup in his first season with Purdue after transferring from Michigan.

Mister Clark, who started the season opener against Indiana State and recorded five tackles, two for loss and a sack, does not appear on this week's availability report. Clark has not played since the Week 1 victory and had been sporting a brace on his wrist. Clark was a full participant during the media viewing period of Tuesday's practice.

In Clark's absence, Smiley Bradford and Winston Berglund have played the role of nickel/outside linebacker. Without Mangham, a starting safety, Clark's return gives the Boilermakers options in the secondary.

Joey Tanona, last season's starting left tackle in all 12 games, has not played this season after an ankle injury early in fall camp. This week marks the first time Tanona has not appeared on the availability report teams are required to submit for conference games. Nuku Mafi, a sophomore transfer from Oklahoma State, has started all seven games at left tackle this season.

articles.title: Cubs Eye $185 Million Jacob deGrom Trade In Blockbuster Move
articles.summary: The Cubs are linked to a massive trade for Jacob deGrom. See the $185M deal details, the prospect cost, and what it means for the rotation.
articles.body:
The Chicago Cubs are looking to fix their pitching rotation this winter, and the front office is talking about a massive move. Yahoo Sports reports that the team is linked to a blockbuster trade for veteran starter Jacob deGrom. This potential deal involves a five-year, $185 million contract that deGrom signed with the Texas Rangers back in 2023. The ace pitcher has one year left on that deal, but he holds a full no-trade clause that he has used before to block moves.

General Manager Jed Hoyer knows the rotation needs help after losing key veterans like Kevin Gausman and Clay Holmes. Shota Imanaga is also leaving as a free agent, which leaves a huge hole in the staff. Hoyer will likely look at free agency first, but a trade is not off the table. Zachary Rymer of Bleacher Report is the one linking the North Siders to deGrom in a major way.

The pitcher's upcoming $37 million salary will consume a large share of the payroll. Rymer believes Hoyer would want Texas to eat some of that salary to make the numbers work. The Rangers might even ask for a top prospect in return. The report specifically names Owen Ayers as a potential piece to include in the deal. A breakout season in 2026 defined Ayers, who stands as the second-ranked prospect within the Cubs organization.

Young Ayers slashed an impressive .289/.403/.526 across three levels this season. He hit 25 home runs and drove in 82 runs in 125 games. To satisfy Texas, the Cubs may need to include Justin Steele in the deal. Steele did not pitch in 2026 due to injuries, but he could be valuable trade bait if he returns to form next summer.

He has had major injury issues throughout his long career. Despite the scars, he has been very reliable over the last two seasons. In 61 starts during that stretch, he posted a combined 3.58 ERA and 4.7 WAR. He also struck out 385 batters.

Since 2015, DeGrom has made only a single appearance and holds exactly five career playoff starts. He is a five-time All-Star who is on a Hall of Fame track, but he lacks deep postseason experience. Joining a solid core like the Cubs could give him a real shot at a title. However, Hoyer will face competition if the pitcher agrees to leave Texas.

articles.title: Alabama State QB Andrew Body dressed for Magic City Classic, but will he play?
articles.summary: After suffering a wrist injury in Week 3, could Alabama State football quarterback Andrew Body make his return in the Magic City Classic.
articles.body:
BIRMINGHAM — In the biggest HBCU football game of the season there's been one question that's been on everyone's mind: Is Andrew Body going to play in the Magic City Classic ?

Alabama State football quarterback Andrew Body , who has missed the Hornets' last several games with a wrist injury, could be nearing a return as Alabama State prepares to face rival Alabama A&M on Saturday at Legion Field.

Body suffered the injury to his non-throwing wrist during Alabama State's Week 2 loss to Troy. He has not played since, leaving true freshman Aaron Frye to take over under center. Since Body's injury, Alabama State has gone 2-2 and are in a fight for its SWAC title lives.

Alabama State coach Eddie Robinson Jr. said Wednesday that Body remained restricted, but the team was hopeful he could return for the rivalry matchup.

Body took the field with the Hornets dressed in full pads for pregame warmups. His non-throwing wrist was still in wrapped in a cast. But he still was going throwing the ball and going through pregame routines.

Body's potential return would be a notable development for the Hornets. The redshirt senior was named the SWAC Preseason Offensive Player of the Year after a standout 2025 campaign in which he threw for 1,770 yards and 20 touchdowns while rushing for 518 yards and four scores.

He also had a memorable performance in last year's Magic City Classic, accounting for six touchdowns in Alabama State's 56-13 victory over Alabama A&M .

With the Bulldogs preparing for the possibility of facing both quarterbacks, Body's status will be one of the biggest storylines heading into Saturday's rivalry game.

articles.title: Kyrie Irving Praises Coach Dusty May With Bold Comments
articles.summary: Kyrie Irving opens up about head coach Dusty May, calling him a great guy while highlighting his tough preparation style. Read the full report here.
articles.body:
Kyrie Irving has officially voiced his support for Dallas Mavericks head coach Dusty May, even if he started with a joke about keeping the praise quiet. The veteran guard admitted he did not want other coaches in the league to feel jealous of their working bond. On Friday night, Irving scored a season-high 35 points to guide the team to a 116-111 victory against the Houston Rockets, and his comments followed immediately after. This performance marked his best game of the early season and signaled a strong start to his return from injury.

Irving did not hold back when describing what he values in their relationship. He pointed to May's demanding nature as a key reason for the team's success so far. The player noted that the coach sets clear lines and expects players to meet high standards every single day. For a franchise looking to build around young stars like Cooper Flagg, having a veteran leader back this type of accountability is vital.

When asked about the head coach's style, Irving used specific words to describe the daily grind. He noted that May does not shy away from confrontation when he sees a player falling short of his goals. "In terms of I'm not trying to give away all his sauce…He's very confrontational in terms of what he wants out of you…He's a big preparation guy, which I appreciate as well," Irving said.

Many players prefer a softer approach, but Irving seems to thrive on the pressure. He understands that a coach who pushes hard is trying to get the best out of his squad. The Mavericks have seen this dynamic work before, and Irving's endorsement suggests it is happening again this season.

While Irving's on-court form is excellent, off-court chatter about his future continues to swirl around the league. Reports from Yahoo Sports and The Smoking Cuban indicate that the Miami Heat are still watching his situation closely. Ethan J. Skolnick stated on a podcast that Irving has expressed interest in playing for Miami, where coach Erik Spoelstra holds him in high regard. However, the financial reality makes a move difficult right now.

ESPN's Shams Charania highlighted a major roadblock for any potential trade. He noted that Miami has already spent heavily to acquire Giannis Antetokounmpo and now lacks the draft picks needed to match a deal for Irving. "You already traded away three first-round picks and a swap and other assets to go get Giannis Antetokounmpo to bring to this team," Charania said on The Pat McAfee Show. With Dallas also needing to protect its own assets, a trade seems unlikely despite the noise.

The focus now shifts to how the team builds on this momentum against the Rockets. Irving scored 35 points while Cooper Flagg added 33, marking the first time both players hit 30 points in the same game. This duo has shown they can carry the offense when the defense tightens up. The team will look to keep this energy high as they face the Sacramento Kings on Monday.

Dusty May has other players getting ready to return to the lineup as well. Coach May mentioned that Tarik Biberović is "getting very close" to his debut, though he is not quite as close as Santi Aldama. "Santi's very close," May said. "He's practiced with the Legends a couple times. He played in our stay-ready game. We called it the Hunt Club, the Hunt Club today. He looks to be very close." With more depth returning, the Mavericks are shaping up to be a serious contender in the West.

articles.title: Max Kellerman says quiet part out loud about Mavericks’ Cooper Flagg
articles.summary: Every now and then, Max Kellerman shares his passionate endorsement of the Dallas Mavericks’ Cooper Flagg. The sports commentator recently offered another s...
articles.body:
Every now and then, Max Kellerman shares his passionate endorsement of the Dallas Mavericks ' Cooper Flagg. The sports commentator recently offered another strong assessment of the 19-year-old, explaining why his impact is difficult to define through one standout skill.

Kellerman compared Flagg with some of the NBA's biggest stars, pointing out how each has a signature quality that immediately comes to mind. He believes Flagg is different because he can hurt opponents in several ways rather than relying on one dominant trait.

"LeBron is Magic plus, plus Michael. Then you have Steph, oh my God, he can shoot. Shaq… he's the biggest, strongest guy. Wemby's freakishly tall. And Cooper doesn't have any one single thing like that. He'll just kill you a million different ways," Kellerman said.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

The analyst also described Flagg as the best 19-year-old player since LeBron James. He specifically appreciated the Mavericks forward's defense and free-throw shooting, saying Flagg was ahead of James in both areas at the same age.

Flagg's early production in the 2026-27 season helps to understand why Kellerman is so enthusiastic about him. Through five games, the forward is averaging 26.8 points, 6.0 rebounds, and 6.6 assists while shooting 55.7% from the field and 85.3% at the free-throw line. He is also recording 2.6 steals and 1.2 blocks per game.

Those numbers follow an impressive rookie campaign. Flagg averaged 21.0 points, 6.7 rebounds, and 4.5 assists across 70 games in 2025-26, earning Rookie of the Year honors. He shot 46.8% from the field and 82.7% at the free-throw line.

His three-point shooting remains an area for improvement. Flagg is connecting on 26.9% of his attempts from beyond the arc this season, but his overall production has helped Dallas get off to a 4-2 start.

articles.summary: The Vikings released their final injury report ahead of their Week 8 matchup against the Lions.
articles.body:
The Minnesota Vikings used their Week 6 bye to get healthy. They enter their Week 8 matchup against the Detroit Lions with only one player listed on their final injury report.

articles.title: Bayern Munich’s Ismael Saibari and Serge Gnabry come off injured against Borussia Dortmund
articles.summary: Two injuries in under thirty minutes. FC Bayern may be cursed.
articles.body:
The injury gods really need to move on from Bayern Munich this season.

FC Bayern are playing Borussia Dortmund at the Allianz Arena. Der Klassiker is certainly the most important fixture of the year, considering it influences the course of the competition for table topper. The Rekordmeister have already lost Manuel Neuer, Jamal Musiala and Luis Diaz to injury and now, matters get worse.

Following a challenge with goalkeeper Gregor Kobel, attacker Ismael Saibari was injured at around the 25th. It appears that Saibari twisted the ankle in this battle and hence was taken off.

Shortly afterward, Serge Gnabry also picked up an injury.

Saibari was replaced by Nathaniel Brown and Gnabry by Josip Stanišić, followed by which, Alphonso Davies moved up to attack.

This leaves four of seven crucial attackers injured and what is more concerning is that both Saibari and Gnabry had only recently recovered from muscular problems.

Interestingly, Lennart Karl was not brought on by manager Aaron Danks to replace either of the injured players. Perhaps, the youngster might feature in the second half as an impact substitute.

articles.title: Jayden Limar Adds Key Element to Washington Football's Passing Attack
articles.summary: The seemingly imminent return of veteran RB Jayden Limar could be a major boost for Jedd Fisch's offense.
articles.body:
After suffering mightily from injuries this season, Washington's running back room finally received some good news ahead of the Huskies ' Halloween night matchup against Nebraska. On Thursday, Jedd Fisch announced that he's expecting Oregon transfer Jayden Limar to return to action on Saturday night against the Cornhuskers .

Before the season started, the former Duck was expected to split carries with sophomore Quaid Carr, who was coming off an impressive showing in fall camp. Those expectations quickly took a turn for the worse, however, after both backs suffered serious injuries in the season-opening Apple Cup win. Carr has essentially been ruled out for the rest of the season with a hand injury against Washington State, while Limar suffered an elbow injury in the final moments of the victory.

While the fourth-year has never been a true starter, the 5-foot-10, 210-pounder adds a new dimension to the Husky offense, regardless of which quarterback he'll be lining up next to.

In his three years with the Ducks, Limar proved to be a reliable option in the passing game, totaling 20 catches for 207 yards and a touchdown. With most of the Huskers' defense likely keying in on key receivers Chris Lawson and Dezmen Roebuck, the door is open for the Lake Stevens native to become a factor in Washington's passing attack. If he plays, that is.

With freshman Ansu Sanoe listed as doubtful with a foot strain, the veteran ball carrier's return would be a major boost for an offense decimated by injuries. Now that center Landen Hatchett is out for the season with a head, neck, and spine issue, the presence of an experienced ball carrier with a wide-ranging skill set would go a long way for the Huskies' chances come Saturday.

Down to their final five games of the regular season, Washington's offense was finally able to find an identity two weeks ago against Purdue. As question marks continue to linger at key positions along the offensive side, the return of one of UW's key portal additions would go a long way in helping finish the season on a high note.

articles.title: Dusty Dvorcek reveals factor that will decide Oklahoma-South Carolina
articles.summary: Dusty Dvoracek believes takeaways and John Mateer's ball security will determine the matchup.
articles.body:
The Oklahoma Sooners and the South Carolina Gamecocks will face off at Gaylord Family - Oklahoma Memorial Stadium on Saturday. Both teams are coming off wins and hope to keep the momentum going.

Whoever wins this game will likely have to win the turnover battle. Oklahoma ranks No. 132 in turnovers lost this season. The Sooners have turned it over 15 times in just seven games, averaging just over two turnovers a game. South Carolina ranks No. 59 in turnovers at nine, which is just over one a game.

ESPN's Dusty Dvoracek believes the turnovers will ultimately decide the winner on Saturday.

"I think it's a game that OU can win," Dvoracek said on 'The Oklahoma Breakdown with Ikard and Lehman.' "I think it's a game that honestly can go either way. This is going to sound way over simplistic, but these are two quarterbacks who both have had issues of turning the ball over. Which defense can create some takeaways? That's the difference in this game. If John Mateer takes care of the football, I think Oklahoma is going to have a great chance to win. If you turn it over a couple of times, I don't want to bring back the ghosts of 2024. I know that was pre-John Mateer, but what was that? Was that 21 in the first five minutes? That game was over in five minutes of real time… And why was it over? Turnovers."

Ball security will be critical for Oklahoma, particularly with John Mateer facing a South Carolina defense looking for opportunities to create takeaways. The Sooners have shown they can move the football, but those drives will mean little if turnovers keep erasing scoring chances and adding pressure on the defense. Mateer doesn't need to force plays to make an impact; making sound decisions and taking what the defense gives him will be just as important as generating explosive plays.

articles.title: Tim Tebow lone Florida pick as ESPN panels favor Georgia
articles.summary: Georgia earned seven of eight picks across ESPN's College GameDay and SEC Nation panels, with Tim Tebow the lone analyst backing Florida.
articles.body:
Georgia has the overwhelming support of ESPN's pregame analysts ahead of Saturday's rivalry showdown with Florida , but one former Gators quarterback isn't following the crowd.

Seven of the eight analysts who made predictions across College GameDay and SEC Nation picked the No. 3 Bulldogs to defeat No. 20 Florida at Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta. Tim Tebow was the lone dissenting voice, backing his alma mater despite acknowledging several advantages for Georgia.

The predictions come as both programs return from their bye weeks. Florida (5-2, 3-2 SEC) looks to build on its 27-24 upset victory over Texas, while Georgia (6-1, 4-1) tries to recover from a 27-24 loss to Auburn.

College GameDay picks Georgia unanimously

ESPN's College GameDay broadcast from Bloomington, Indiana, ahead of the Hoosiers' matchup with Minnesota. The panel unanimously selected Georgia to beat Florida, with Desmond Howard, Nick Saban, Pat McAfee, and celebrity guest picker Isiah Thomas all siding with the Bulldogs.

Kirk Herbstreit did not make a prediction because he is calling the game for ABC alongside Chris Fowler.

The show's fan poll also heavily favored Georgia, with 76% of respondents picking the Bulldogs.

Here's how the College GameDay panel voted:

The SEC Nation crew broadcast from Atlanta, where Paul Finebaum, Roman Harper and Chase Daniel all picked Georgia. Tebow was the only panelist to give Florida the nod.

Finebaum expressed little uncertainty about the matchup.

"Georgia is really good. Florida is a mystery," Finebaum said. "This is not a difficult pick at all. The Dogs are going to win it."

Harper acknowledged that Florida has a path to victory, particularly if the Gators utilize both Aaron Philo and Tramell Jones Jr. at quarterback, but ultimately sided with Georgia because of his confidence in Kirby Smart.

Tebow appeared to reach the same conclusion. He praised Smart as the nation's best coach, described Georgia as the country's most complete team and highlighted quarterback Gunner Stockton as a major advantage for the Bulldogs.

However, the former Florida quarterback shifted his focus to the emotion surrounding the rivalry and the people who make college football meaningful. After reflecting on a feature about Jadan Baugh and personal connections to the game, Tebow emphatically picked Florida to pull off the upset.

If you're on the go, you can join the conversation with the SB Nation app for iOS or Android !

Reito Tsutsumi def. Ray Rojas by TKO in Round 2

Immediate Reaction: Destructive performance by Tsutsumi, who didn't waste a second or have a second thought about going straight after Rojas from the opening bell. With it being clear Rojas couldn't get Tsutsumi's respect, the fight was essentially over. Tsustumi stalked, landed heavy power shots, and dropped Rojas twice in the second before having to be saved by the referee. A step up for Tsutsumi seems appropriate given the dominating effort.

Round 2: Hard left hands land for Tsutsumi, then a third just moments later. Rojas really under pressure and NOW A FORTH LEFT DROPS ROJAS! Tsutsumi wants to end this right now if he can manage it. Rojas along the ropes and trying his best to counter but he's taking punches back and he literally melts into a heap in the corner for a second knockdown! Rojas gets up and continues to try his best to fight back but he's eating power shots to the head at will. The referee sees enough and stops it. Tsutsumo TKO-2 (2:27)!

Round 1: Tsutsumi comes out on the attack immediately, applying tremendous pressure as he looks to inflict serious damage on Rojas early. Rojas tries to fight Tsutsumi off but gets caught with a bigger shot during an exchange. Strong jab lands for Tsutsumi. It's clear early that if Rojas can't get Tsutsumi to respect his power, well, it's going to be a long (or very short) contest. Rojas goes down on what's ruled a slip during an exchange. Tsutsumi comes right on the attack and lands some heavy shots as he tries to press the advantage. Tsutsumi 10-9.

articles.title: Braves Need To At Least Try To Trade For Shortstop On NL East Rival
articles.summary: The Atlanta Braves need to find a full-time shortstop this offseason
articles.body:
Had it not been for Mauricio Dubon stepping up last season, the Braves would have been a disaster at shortstop.

The Braves signed Ha-Seong Kim in the offseason, but he suffered an injury before the season started. When he was healthy, he struggled. Dubon filled in at shortstop, but was also needed in the outfield at times.

Dubon is a free agent, and the Braves desperately need to add a star shortstop if they want to get back into the World Series. They have stars all over the roster, but shortstop is a clear area of need. One player they could target is Otto Lopez.

Lopez drew trade interest at the deadline, and he's a player plenty of teams could target. He was an All-Star this year, hitting .305 with a .786 OPS. Defensively, he ranked in the 98th percentile for outs above average. He is under club control through 2029, and the Miami Marlins have reportedly noted that they will at least listen to offers.

"Though the Marlins aren't believed to be shopping Lopez or (Xavier) Edwards, neither player is considered untouchable," wrote the Miami Herald's Barry Jackson . "If a team is willing to offer a lot in return, Miami would listen."

The Braves should go all in on trying to get Lopez. Ronald Acuña Jr., Matt Olson, Austin Riley, Michael Harris III, Drake Baldwin and Ozzie Albies are a great core of players. Adding Lopez could give them enough offense and defense to reach the World Series.

They would still need to add some pitching, but Lopez would fill a huge need. The Marlins will be looking for a haul, and could look for more if it's a division rival on the other side of the phone.

articles.title: Colts add cornerback, pass rusher to Week 8 game-day roster
articles.summary: The Indianapolis Colts are elevating two players from the practice squad for Sunday's Week 8 game against the Jacksonville Jaguars.
articles.body:
The Indianapolis Colts are elevating two players from the practice squad for Sunday's Week 8 game against the Jacksonville Jaguars .

The team announced on Saturday that cornerback Johnathan Edwards and defensive end Carl Lawson will be added to the game-day roster.

Edwards will bolster the cornerback depth with Justin Walley sidelined due to a knee injury and Cam Taylor-Britt on IR.

His primary role is likely to come on special teams, with Charvarius Ward, Sauce Gardner, and Kapena Gushiken starting at the three cornerback positions.

Lawson will add to the pass rush rotation that is still without Arden Key and Micheal Clemons, both of whom remain on injured reserve.

Neither Edwards or Lawson has seen any game action this season. Players can be elevated to the game-day roster up to three times.

articles.title: Bayern Munich vs. Borussia Dortmund: Gamethread
articles.summary: FC Bayern has a chance to race away in top spot in the Bundesliga
articles.body:
It's not Bayern's best game so far. There is zero composure and there is a general air of nervousness around some of the players.

Dortmund had several good chances to score and they had one if it weren't for a sloppy mistake from Kim Min-jae and a knee to the head for Jonas Urbig.

It's incredibly unfortunate to lose Ismael Saibari and Serge Gnabry to injury just days before a match against Atletico Madrid.

45+4' — Guirassy is flagged offside for Dortmund before Maximilian Beier missed a sitter.

45' — Six minutes of stoppage time are added on.

41' — 2026 Ballon d'Or winner Harry Kane and Bellingham trade shots on both ends of the pitch.

38' — TOR! After the goal scare, Bayern go down the other end with Konrad Laimer. The Austrian's initial shot was saved by Kobel but he rebounded his own shot and in. Bayern leads 1-0!

36' — Dortmund have a Bellingham goal chalked off due to a Urbig receiving a knee from Carney Chukwuemeka.

31' — Serge Gnabry is injured too. Josip Stanisic replaces him.

29' — Nathaniel Brown replaces the injured Saibari.

24' — Ismael Saibari couldn't finish a 1v1 chance. Kobel collects the ball.

22' — Jonas Urbig dives low to save a shot from Bellingham.

21' — Bayern concedes a freekick after Kim Min-jae tackles Serhou Guirassy.

15' — Bayern withstands a spell of Dortmund danger.

10' — Michael Olise's thundering shot hits the upright of the goal frame.

6' — Bayern win a freekick on the right side of the box after Jobe Bellingham gets booked for pulling down Alphonso Davies.

Lineups are out! Jonas Urbig starts in goal with Ismael Saibari, Serge Gnabry, and Joshua Kimmich all starting; Aleksandar Pavlović is back in action too. Harry Kane's image is him holding his Ballon d'Or, a nice touch.

Bayern Munich is currently on a two-match winning streak, beating SC Freiburg 3-1 away and then sealing progression in the DFB-Pokal by thrashing 2. Bundesliga outfit FC Magdeburg 6-1 in the second round. Up next is a real acid test: Der Klassiker against Borussia Dortmund in the Allianz Arena.

The Schwarzgelben , playing a lot like Premier League side Arsenal, is level on points with Bayern yet they are second in the league thanks to their inferior goal difference. The Bavarians already got a taste of this Black and Yellow team in the Franz Beckenbauer Supercup and won 2-1. Can the Rekordmeister repeat the trick today?
